designSummary: Non-randomised feasibility study with descriptive estimates and pre-specified progression criteria.
sampleSize: About 180 triggered patients are expected on two wards in six months. A delivery proportion of 80 percent would have a 95 percent confidence interval of about 6 percentage points either side; 45 double-rated notes estimate kappa with a standard error of about 0.08, enough to tell whether it clears 0.6. About 60 deaths are expected, so a family response of 34 percent would come from about 20 families; response is reported with its interval, not tested.
primaryAnalysis: Proportion of triggered patients reached by the intervention with 95 percent interval, against the progression criterion of 80 percent.
secondaryAnalysis: Kappa with 95 percent interval; family response by route and deprivation; descriptive change in documentation and mean quality against the 2025 baseline; staff minutes per patient.
missingData: Missing notes and unreturned questionnaires are counted and reported; no imputation in a feasibility study.
multiplicity: No hypothesis tests; progression criteria are judged together.
software: R for descriptive estimates; spreadsheet for the rating log.
overfittingGuards: No effect claims from uncontrolled change
summary: Descriptive estimates against progression criteria; about 180 patients and 45 double-rated notes.
